issues.problem: A hidden Grip part can steer the measure's reference and change a tier. This is Reviewer V1's finding (b); I reproduced it with my own construction (work/speck.luau, out/speck_P5.txt). Sampling.ranked places parts from gripPlace(parts, gripSlot, nil), the point of every Grip part, hidden ones included. The case: P5 (comb blade) with its grip Block (0.16 x 0.9 x 0.16 at the origin) copied 4e-9, or 2e-8, along +X. The verdict keeps one of the two copies by place. A 0.02-stud Grip speck (Dust, so cleaned) inside the grip at x = +0.03 moves that point past the copies' midpoint, and the verdict then keeps the copy instead of the original. The kept Grip point, which is the measure's reference (§4.5), moves 4e-9, P5's twin teeth about x = 0 reorder in the measure, and Hammering goes 0.2167 Hard -> 0.1902 Normal. With no speck, or with the speck at -0.03, it reads 0.2167 Hard. f7ac37d reads 0.2167 Hard in all 9 cases, so this is a regression for such designs. It makes §4.4's 'no cleaned part moves it' (the measure's rank) false. It also goes beyond what §4.4, §5's promise, §5.6's near-copy row, §17.1 O11 (j) and §17.2 say (which near copy is kept, 'G the same', 'none moves'). My own hidden Grip block (out/hgkept_live.txt) also changes the kept sets of X01, X01raw and X02.

A whole-design Y move still changes G where two twin parts' heights differ in the last bit. This is Reviewer V1's finding (a); I reproduced it (work/twins.luau, out/tw_live.txt, out/p5n_*.txt). Both rank keys compare p.cy raw. Two parts tied on volume and slot whose heights differ by one ulp are therefore ordered by height. A move that rounds the two heights to the same value hands the tie to the place, and the order flips. The case: P5 with tooth 6 typed at 1.6000000000000003 (tooth 7 is at 1.6000000000000001) reads Hammering 0.2117. Moved along Y by +0.4007, +0.4030, +0.4110 or +0.4230 (and, for teeth 14 and 15 at 3.4000000000000004, by +0.6007 to +0.6770), it reads 0.2167. That is 9 of 155 Y moves, dG 0.0050, and f7ac37d does the same. V1 measured 857 of 20,676 plausible designs given such twins moving under a slide, 5 of them a tier. These statements are made false, and none of them names this case: §0.5's factors row ('a whole design moved along Y or Z ... every step to the bit'), §5's promise (every step's g and tier to the bit but (h) and (k)), §5.6's Y/Z row, §16.18's shift-fix guards row ('a move along Y or Z keeps every step to the bit'), §16.32's TOL_G_INVARIANT row, and O11 (j)'s list of what remains.

summary:
The fix does what it claims for designs the corpora hold, but two majors stand. Both were found by Reviewer V1 and I reproduced each with my own construction:
1. A hidden Grip speck can decide which copy of a duplicated grip the verdict keeps. That moves the measure's reference and turns P5's Hammering from Hard (0.2167) to Normal (0.1902), where f7ac37d reads 0.2167. This makes §4.4's 'no cleaned part moves it' false.
2. Twin parts whose heights differ in the last bit still let a whole-design Y move change G (P5 nudged: 9 of 155 moves, 0.0050; the same on f7ac37d). This contradicts the SPEC's 'Y/Z to the bit' in §0.5, §5, §5.6, §16.18, §16.32 and O11 (j).

One combined repair, tried in var/vby, closes both: the verdict's places read from the centre of the box of every part but Dust, both ranks key the height in RANK_Q, one Verdict test is adapted and two new pins added. It changes no reading on any corpus (33,389 plausible, 136 fixtures, 200 generated, 500 seed) and passes --quick (718).
